\begin{document}
\title{A Toy Oscillator}
\maketitle
\begin{abstract}
We derive the energy levels of a toy oscillator.
\end{abstract}

\section{Introduction}
We study a harmonic oscillator.

\section{Model}\label{sec:model}
The Hamiltonian is
\begin{equation}\label{eq:H}
H = \frac{p^2}{2m} + \frac{1}{2} m \omega^2 x^2 .
\end{equation}

\section{Derivation}\label{sec:deriv}
Introducing $a = \sqrt{m\omega/2\hbar}\,(x + i p/m\omega)$, Eq.~\eqref{eq:H} becomes
\begin{equation}\label{eq:Ha}
H = \hbar\omega\left(a^\dagger a + \tfrac12\right).
\end{equation}
Using $[a, a^\dagger] = 1$ we find
\begin{equation}\label{eq:comm}
[H, a^\dagger] = \hbar\omega\, a^\dagger .
\end{equation}
Combining \eqref{eq:Ha} and \eqref{eq:comm},
\begin{equation}\label{eq:E}
E_n = \hbar\omega\left(n + \tfrac12\right).
\end{equation}

\section{Conclusion}
The spectrum is equally spaced.
